source.citation: Unidentified author, article on douche treatment, Case II, Medical Record 43 (January 21, 1893): 72–73. Author and title to confirm from the page image.

complaints: unable to apply his mind to business
presentation.course: Treated three years earlier in Paris with douches prescribed by Charcot and stayed well. Broke down again after a crisis in his business and trouble in his family.
presentation.priorTreatment: Four months of douches in Paris, with lasting benefit until the relapse.

findings: not at first strong enough for the cold, high-pressure douche he asked for

treatments.treatment: preparatory warm douche ending with cold water to the spine, and massage
treatments.response: made him fit for the stronger treatment

treatments.treatment: cold column douche at 50°F and two atmospheres along the spine and to the feet, then a cold sheet rub, for six weeks
treatments.response: insomnia gone, appetite improved; returned to business and stayed well

quotes: until a crisis in his busi- ness and family troubles caused him to again break down
His insomnia disappeared, and his appetite steadily improved.

modernReading.text: Probably a depressive or stress-related episode set off by business and family crises, with insomnia and poor concentration. The ritual, structure, and expectation of a treatment that had worked before may explain much of the response.

fixed: relapse after a business and family crisis
prior good response to the same treatment
patient asks for a specific treatment

constrained.rule: elite or affluent; has travelled to Europe for treatment

notes: Useful for a patient who arrives with a fixed idea of the treatment he wants, and whose belief in it matters.
